attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, introducing a tweet of his that MarketWatch quoted. He endorses it in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps his 'strong sign' wording and leaves out the scope added in the earlier draft. 'Strong sign' is a firm inference, not a probability hedge, so the claim is an observation: skepticism is rising.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. Using April 2026 as the period is the evaluator's choice but is reasonable given 'Sunday' and 'today'. The unspecified audience and comparison baseline leave the result dependent on interpretation.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous Guardian recap confirms that Last Week Tonight aired a segment critical of AI chatbots. It does not name Marcus or measure any trend in skepticism, so it is context only.

HSBC investor survey (fieldwork Mar 16–Apr 10, published before the cutoff) reports investor enthusiasm becoming more discriminating. This partly supports rising skepticism about AI economics among investors only, and the survey also reports continued enthusiasm.
Gallup's Gen Z survey shows worsening AI sentiment compared with 2025, but fieldwork ended in March and it covers only one age group's general attitudes. Trend context only.

Just Capital reports rising optimism among the public and investors between Fall 2025 and early 2026. This counts against the claim, but fieldwork came before April and it asks a different question, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: No usable evidence shows that either outlet featured Marcus's warnings. The trend evidence is split: HSBC finds investors more discriminating, Gallup finds Gen Z more negative, and Just Capital finds optimism rising. These surveys cover different populations, questions and periods. The support condition is not met and the contradiction condition is not established, so the packet does not settle the outcome.
